Restart-when: `npm view @objectstack/spec version` answers a release whose `AutomationResult` declares `flowLabel` (objectstack PR #20633), and objectui `main`'s `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves it

## Triage: first grade — `enhancement` · `priority:p3` · `domain:ui` · `area:i18n` · `pm:on-hold`. It is held on the install surface: the middle step of the label chain is not in any spec objectui can install

Triage: lands in `FlowRunner.tsx` (in `app-shell`), the one component both hosts mount ⇒ `domain:ui`. It takes the p3 and `area:i18n` of its parent, objectstack-ai/objectstack#20318.

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-09-29T12:58Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

**Why held, not queued.**
- The chain the parent's direction sets is: the active locale's `translation.flows.FLOW.label`, then `flowLabel`, then `flowName`.
- `flowLabel` is declared by objectstack PR #20633 (`AutomationResult.flowLabel`, and mirrored in `TriggerFlowResponseSchema.data`). It merged at 2026-09-29T12:25Z, but it isn't in any published release: npm's latest is `17.5.0`, and objectui's lockfile resolves `17.4.0`.
- So reading it now means a local type for a field the installed contract doesn't have, which is the consumer-side widening objectui's AGENTS.md bans.
- The card is small enough to land whole once the release is installable. ⛔ Don't split it into a translation-only PR now and a second one later.

**Direction at restart** (the card body's "What the reader does" stands):
- `ScreenFlowState` keeps `flowLabel` from the trigger and resume responses.
- The runner header and the completion toast show the resolved label; the toast shows it in place of the API name.
- **Pins:** a zh bundle, an en fallback, and a flow with no translation showing its authored label.
- **After landing:** objectstack-ai/objectstack#20318 flips its ledger row when the objectstack console pin moves past this card (#20638 is the current pin-bump card).

## Hold released: `pm:on-hold` → `pm:queue`. The `Restart-when:` condition (this card's 2026-09-29 triage grade) holds on the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.6.0

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-05T00:08Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. Found in a full pass over blocked and held cards.

**The condition:** "`npm view @objectstack/spec version` answers a release whose `AutomationResult` declares `flowLabel` (objectstack PR #20633), and objectui `main`'s `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves it."

**Readings at this write:**
- `@objectstack/spec@17.6.0` from npm, unpacked: `dist/contracts/index.d.ts` `interface AutomationResult` declares `flowLabel?: string`. `TriggerFlowResponse`'s data schema in `dist/automation-api.zod-*.d.ts` carries `flowLabel: z.ZodOptional<z.ZodString>`.
- objectui `origin/main` `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves `@objectstack/spec` at `17.6.0` only (since objectui#11438 / PR #11531).

**So the hold could have released when objectui moved to 17.6.0 (2026-10-03).** The grade in this card's triage comment stands: `enhancement` · p3 · `domain:ui` · `area:i18n`. objectstack-ai/objectstack#20318 is blocked on this card, and it unlocks when this one closes.

Why `Clause-②: yes`: `ScreenFlowState` is exported from `@object-ui/app-shell` (`src/index.ts:224`), and the card's direction adds `flowLabel` to it. That widens a published type.

## ACCEPT (content): PR objectui#11636, head `6950ab0`. The contract review is still owed before landing

`domain:ui` execution seat 1 @ objectui · `session_015W8GBu6sBiqus2L2xjMsAL` (`os-steve`) · 2026-10-05T02:42Z. Reviewed against GitHub and `origin/main`, not against the report's prose (`os-dev-report` on this card).

- **Shape.** The PR is a draft against `main`, and its assignee is `os-steve`. Its first line is `Fixes #11092`, the only line with a closing keyword next to an issue number. `Clause-②: yes` is on its own line. Against `main` the diff is 11 files, +438/−19, inside the claim's file surface.
- **The label is read once and typed by the contract.** `interpretFlowResponse` lifts `flowLabel` in one place (`servedFlowLabel`) onto the `paused` and `done` arms and onto `judgeFlowLaunch`'s `screen` follow-up. Every new member is `Pick<AutomationResult, 'flowLabel'>` from the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.6.0, with no local re-declaration. The resolution order is the card's (bundle, then served label, then API name), and its first two steps are the spec's own `translateFlow` over the bundle the runner already reads.
- **Zone 2 #2 held:** the card named two hosts, and there are three. `FlowRunsPage.tsx` threads the label at both of its open sites, with a pin.
- **Display slot (the card left it open):** a muted line above the screen heading names the flow. The heading stays the step's own title and the dialog's accessible name. The completion toast passes the resolved label as the existing `flowRunner.completed` key's `flow` parameter, so no i18n key is added.
- **Changeset, sentence by sentence.** `@object-ui/app-shell: minor` and `@object-ui/console: patch` match what the diff publishes. The "older server" paragraph matches the code: with no served label and no bundle entry, both slots show the API name. The `Clause-②` paragraph names the one widened member, `ScreenFlowState.flowLabel`, and says no prop, export or i18n key moves. That matches the diff.
- **Tests.** The pins cover the zh bundle, the en served label, an untranslated flow, no label at all, a paused resume, and one pin per host. Two ablation legs went red exactly where predicted. The whole `app-shell` suite was green before the merge. After the merge, one unrelated file (`AppContent.deniedVsUnpublished.test.tsx`, not in this diff) tripped the network-escape guard under whole-package load, and it passed run alone. CI on this head is the verdict on it.

**Owed before landing:** an isolated review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this head, because the claim declares `Clause-②: yes`. `needs:contract-review` is added to the PR in this stroke. The PR stays a draft until a conforming PASS is on record and every check on the head is green.
